constraint_decided_it: P141 assigned (E13 -> E1) declares that the range entity 'plays the role of the range of the attribution'; the entity that RECEIVED the attribution is reached by P140 assigned attribute to ('plays the role of the domain of the attribution'), which is also what P1's FOL shortcut fixes: P1(x,y) <= (Ex z)[E15(z) & P140i(x,z) & P37(z,y)]. Answer A writes 'P37 assigned the E42 56, P141 assigned it to that A8 instance', putting the stratigraphic unit in P141's range slot -- the same slot its own subproperty P37 already fills with the E42. Answer B never makes that inversion; it omits P140 rather than misusing P141.
better_modelling: Two units, not one, and each at its most specific CRMarchaeo class: the Trench 3 posthole cut is an A3 Stratigraphic Interface (A3's scope note covers surfaces 'formed by the removal or destruction of existing stratifications'), the Trench 7 fill an A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit. Two distinct E42 Identifiers, each P190 has symbolic content '56' (E62) -- distinct appellation instances with equal content, which is what lets the strings collide without any co-reference claim -- each P1 is identified by its own unit. Two E15 Identifier Assignments, each P140 assigned attribute to its unit, P37 assigned its E42, P14 carried out by the supervisor, P4 has time-span the 1978 season; optionally each context sheet as an E31 Document P70 documents its unit. No L54 is same as, no A6 Group Declaration Event. t0154 (issue 103) supplies the direct archive warrant neither answer found: Doerr's redraft of the E42 scope note states an identifier 'may come out of use, and, by chance, it may be reused for another object'.
reasoning: Both answers reach the right top-level call -- two entities, an identifier collision rather than an identity problem -- and both correctly ground it in E42's 'uniquely and permanently within the context of one or more organisations' (verbatim) plus P1's (0,n:0,n) quantification (verbatim), so the split is entirely in the construction. A misidentifies the relationship between the E15 and the unit it documents, using P141 where P140 is the declared property, and compounds it by leaving both units at the generic A8 when A2 and A3 are the applicable specialisations. B gets A2 for the fill, verifies and correctly rules out A6 against its actual scope note (which does list postholes-as-a-past-house and units cut by a ditch as its examples), and its one archive quote, t0633 'He issued identifiers', is verbatim; its defects are omission -- no P140 to close the fully developed path, no A3 for the posthole cut -- not error. A's remaining flaws are softer: issue 427 is cited but concerns the SIG's policy on reusing deprecated CRM class/property numbers, not identifier collision in a site archive, and the inference that P1/P48's absence from A8's Required block shows the model treats identifiers as 'incidental' is unsound, since P1 is required on no class at all.
